title: Utilizing Federally Funded Clinics / Mental Health, Substance Disorder and Crisis Care Needs / People Experiencing Homelessness
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the Council instruct the City Administrative Officer and the Chief Legislative Analyst, with assistance from the City Attorney, the Los Angeles Housing Department, and other relevant departments, to report on a strategy for pursuing federal funding and utilizing federally funded clinics to meet the mental health, substance use disorder, and crisis care needs of people . . experiencing homelessness in the City, including: wee— 1. An inventory of federally funded clinics operating in or serving the City, including FQHCs, Health Care for the Homeless grantees, FQHC Look-Alikes, and CCBHCs, with their service sites, capacity, and the behavioral health services each provides to PEH; OCT 1 4 2026 2. The scope of mental health, substance use disorder, and crisis services these clinics can provide and bill for through federal grants, Medi-Cal, and Medicare independent of County contracts, and any services that remain under the County's exclusive authority; 3. Options for the City to partner directly with existing clinics; 4. State or federal funding opportunities available to expand clinic capacity in the City and whether the City or a City-created entity could qualify for state or federal health center funding; 5. Cost estimates for a pilot program placing clinic services at City homelessness program sites; and 6. The City's legal authority to establish its own behavioral health department or jurisdiction, similar to the City of Berkeley and the Tri-City Mental Health Authority. I FURTHER MOVE that the Council instruct the City Administrative Officer, with assistance from the Chief Legislative Analyst and the City Attorney, to report on options to establish dedicated healthcare expertise to support the City's homelessness programs and policies, including through in-house staff and consulting services, with expertise in healthcare systems, policy, financing, and service delivery. I FURTHER MOVE that the Council instruct the City Administrative Officer, with assistance from the Chief Legislative Analyst, to identify and evaluate any other funding options available to support mental health, substance use disorder, and healthcare services for people experiencing homelessness in the City, including federal, state, County, and philanthropic sources.
